name: n8n
summary: n8n is a visual workflow tool that connects your app to other services, and you can use n8n's cloud or run it on your own server.

free_plan_covers.note: The cloud Free plan includes 50 workflow runs a month and 1 user, enough to try things out. The self-hosted Community edition is free with no run limit, but you pay for and look after the server yourself.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The cloud Starter plan is 24 a month billed monthly (20 a month billed yearly) for 2,500 workflow runs. n8n lists its prices in euros, so the dollar amount on your card can differ a little.

portability.note: You can move between n8n's cloud and your own server, but workflows are built from n8n's own nodes and only run inside n8n, so leaving n8n means rebuilding them.

self_hostable.note: The Community edition runs on your own server for free, with full control over setup. Some team features need a paid license.

code_steps.note: The Code node runs JavaScript or Python. On n8n's cloud you can't add outside libraries (JavaScript only gets crypto and moment); on your own server you can.

webhook_triggers.note: The Webhook node gives each workflow a web address your app can call. It has a test address for building and a production address that works once the workflow is published.

setup.step: Create an n8n Cloud account, or install the free Community edition on your own server.
Start the workflow with a Webhook node, publish it, and copy its production address into your app's environment file.

builder_notes: Call the n8n webhook from server code only, and read its address from N8N_WEBHOOK_URL instead of writing it into the page.
Use the production webhook address in the deployed app; the test address only works while someone is listening in the editor.
Keep service logins in n8n's credentials, not typed into workflow steps.
